headline: High risk: Windsurf’s broad filesystem/MCP/network defaults can leak or corrupt EMQX IoT workspaces, while shared local files create prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use clipboard, and connect to MCP servers, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions. EMQX exposes HTTP API and broad network egress, but no direct ingestion channel is documented; the pairwise bridge is inferred from Windsurf’s local-file/MCP surfaces.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs are copied into a shared workspace file or MCP-fed artifact
IF Windsurf is configured to auto-apply instructions from file or MCP content
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Keep EMQX outputs in a separate, read-only directory
Strip instructions from any shared artifacts before opening them
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between EMQX outputs and Windsurf inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard, and can send content through model proxy or MCP servers. Shared local files make leakage plausible in default workflows, though the exact data path is indirect and not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is stored in the same workspace that Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf forwards file contents or clipboard contents to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Store sensitive EMQX data outside the Windsurf workspace
Turn off clipboard-based sharing for sensitive sessions
Review MCP server allowlists before use
Redact IoT payloads before opening them in Windsurf
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive workspaces with OS-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem; EMQX is network-capable and may also manipulate files indirectly through its HTTP API. The shared mutable workspace plus git/file writes creates a direct conflict pathway, and uncertainty about EMQX’s write scope should escalate rather than downgrade.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-commits or EMQX writes artifacts into that workspace
mitigations: Use separate worktrees for each agent
Disable auto-commit and auto-apply in Windsurf
Lock the repository before either agent writes
Keep EMQX outputs out of git-tracked paths
requires-engineering: add cross-agent file locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s single-agent loop and tool use can treat upstream artifacts as authoritative, and EMQX can emit operational data over HTTP. If EMQX-generated content is fed into Windsurf without verification, Windsurf may propagate or act on incorrect facts; the pairwise interaction is plausible in default file-based workflows, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF EMQX output is used as input to Windsurf tasks without a verification step
IF Windsurf is allowed to execute commands based on that unverified output
mitigations: Require human review before Windsurf acts on EMQX-derived facts
Add a verification checklist for any EMQX-generated artifact
Separate data extraction from action-taking steps
Disable auto-execute for tasks sourced from EMQX outputs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for EMQX-to-Windsurf handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while Windsurf handles source code, open files, and model-provider keys with broad network egress. If IoT payloads include regulated personal data and are opened in Windsurf, residency or retention mismatches can arise; only EMQX is directly tied to the data class, so the second citation is unnecessary here.
conditions: IF IoT data contains regulated personal data or secrets
IF that data is opened or retained in Windsurf workspaces or model calls
mitigations: Keep regulated IoT data out of Windsurf sessions
Review Windsurf retention and logging settings
Use synthetic or redacted datasets for coding tasks
Confirm data residency requirements before sharing artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based data loss prevention on workspace files
